draft.title: European Express Meets a Mixed Market
draft.description: Our reading of Goldman’s European Express: data-center power, telcos, trucks and policy meet a mixed market backdrop with clear crosscurrents.
draft.body_html:
Research Desk — Mastermind Research

What the desk argued

Mastermind Research’s coverage of Goldman Sachs’ 8-page European Express, published on 2026-09-23, brings together several distinct business cases under a macro lens. The clearest growth claim concerns behind-the-meter power for data centers: the desk sees a $55bn cumulative equipment opportunity by 2030 alongside a 67GW forecast for this power market.

That argument rests on execution rather than on demand alone. Ceres Power, Weichai Power and Delta Electronics are presented as companies positioned to benefit if projects move from planning into delivered capacity. The report also frames European telecom consolidation as a source of modest cost efficiency gains, while retaining a constructive view across DT, United Internet, 1&1, Ionos and Vodafone.

Elsewhere, the desk highlights replacement-driven North American demand for Daimler Truck and describes a 15-20% discount against Chinese OEMs. Its case includes feasible peak margins and an operational target for Torc’s autonomous work. On macro conditions, it points to core PCE slowing to 2.5% annualized and interprets the Fed’s departure from its no-hike forecast as a softer turn for rate expectations and asset values.

The common thread is that company-specific execution, consolidation and replacement demand may matter even when the broader setting remains unsettled. Our coverage page sets out the full desk read.

What our data says

Our market-state composite was 50 of 100, or MIXED, on 2026-10-12. That reading supports restraint around broad claims: the Trend & technicals component scored 70, but Breadth & participation scored 0. Stronger directional conditions therefore coexist with very limited participation.

Risk appetite scored 27 on 2026-10-12, while the volatility backdrop scored 84. The difference matters for the report’s execution-heavy themes. A favorable backdrop for some market mechanics does not establish a uniformly receptive environment for every growth or consolidation thesis.

The breadth split is particularly relevant to the data-center power argument. As of 2026-10-08, 62.3% of the AI cohort stood above its 50-day average, compared with 27.0% of the non-AI cohort. The 35.3 point spread shows that participation was concentrated rather than broadly shared.

Our risk radar remained in caution on 2026-10-12, with rates the dominant scare at 70.3 and a modelled 21-session drawdown probability of 0.19. That does not contradict the report’s lower-rate interpretation, but it does show that rate sensitivity remains the live fault line rather than a settled tailwind.

Dealer positioning also separates large-cap support from smaller-company fragility. SPX dealer gamma was 76.9bn net on 2026-10-08, while IWM was -4.45bn net and RUT was -2.51bn net. That contrast agrees with a selective reading of the desk’s themes and argues against treating them as one uniform market call.

What would change the picture

A broader improvement in participation would strengthen the case that the report’s opportunities are becoming less concentrated. Conversely, persistently weak breadth alongside low risk appetite would leave the current mixed assessment intact even if the 67GW power opportunity remains compelling on paper.

For the macro portion, a change in the rates signal would be decisive. The current 2.5% core PCE observation and the caution reading can coexist, but a clearer shift in either direction would alter how much weight to place on valuation support. For the company themes, evidence that execution, cost savings and replacement demand are translating into durable results would matter more than a general market move. For now, the appropriate conclusion is watch, do not chase.
